report.answer: A basketball drifts in a straight line at constant speed with no fall — it is in free-floating weightlessness, not a throw on Earth. Projectile fit gives essentially zero vertical acceleration, so the path is a straight inertial trajectory at ~0.96 m/s angled ~21° above horizontal. Yellow measured centres and cyan fit coincide to sub-pixel.
assumptions: motion roughly in a plane facing the camera
basketball diameter 0.24 m at same depth as motion

forks.label: Earth gravity
forks.why: Same throw on Earth would arc down into parabola.

forks.label: Moon gravity
forks.why: Same throw would show gentle 1.62 m/s2 parabola.

derived.name: launch_angle
derived.desc: angle above horizontal at first sample

derived.name: apex_height
derived.desc: highest y reached (in the same frame as y)

derived.name: g_if_rolling_sphere
derived.desc: g implied if this is a solid sphere rolling without slipping: a = (5/7) g sin(alpha)

derived.name: g_if_sliding_frictionless
derived.desc: g implied for a frictionless sliding block: a = g sin(alpha)

derived.name: mu_if_sliding_on_earth
derived.desc: kinetic friction coefficient if a sliding block on Earth (g = 9.81): mu = tan(alpha) - a / (g cos(alpha))

derived.name: terminal_velocity
derived.desc: sqrt(g/b): speed at which drag balances gravity (null if b <= 0)

derived.name: omega
derived.desc: angular frequency of the damped oscillation

derived.name: damping_time
derived.desc: 1/gamma: amplitude e-folding time (null if not damped)

derived.name: Q
derived.desc: quality factor omega_n / (2 gamma) (null if not damped)

events.text: Motion looks weightless — checking the visual overlay to confirm.
